captions.text: Recap of chapter 13: the agent now talks to a Model class, not to Ollama.
Message and ToolCall are the framework's own format.
OllamaModel translates to and from Ollama's format, at the edge.
And FakeModel lets tests run with no model at all.
Today's black box: the tool system.
Let's open it.
Each tool is written twice: a function, and a schema. Let's make them disagree.
Rename path to filename in the function, and leave the schema alone.
Predict: what will the model send now?
Listing the folder works. Then read_file fails.
The model sees only the schema, so it keeps sending path.
Nothing warned us, and the run used up all its steps.
Python already knows a lot about a function. This script is provided.
Predict: which part of a schema can't Python tell you?
__annotations__ gives the types.
__doc__ gives the description.
A parameter with no default is a required one.
Only one thing is missing: a description for each parameter.
Annotated holds a type and a note. Python ignores the note.
But your program can read it back.
This function turns a signature into a schema.
It goes through the parameters, as peek.py did.
It splits each hint into a type and a description.
No Annotated hint? Then it stops with an error, on purpose.
No default? Then the parameter is required.
The decorator gives back a Tool: the schema's parts, plus the function.
__call__ means a Tool can still be called like a function.
And @tool builds it all from the function you already wrote.
Now make the same mistake here. There's no second copy to forget.
Predict: what will the model send this time?
It sends filename. The schema changed with the function.
The same edit that stalled chapter 13's agent now does no harm.
So why is a missing description an error? This is chapter 11's test again.
Predict: without descriptions, which path will it choose?
With descriptions, it chose the real path 5 times out of 5.
Without them, it made up a name 5 times out of 5. So @tool insists.
A Toolbox holds the tools, and it's the only thing that runs them.
An unknown tool gets a list of the real ones.
New here: check compares the arguments with the schema first.
And a tool that raises an error still comes back as text.
Here are five calls, as a confused model might send them. No model is involved.
Predict: will any of them crash the program?
The first is fine. The second names a tool that doesn't exist.
A missing argument, and then an unknown one.
A missing file. Nothing crashed, and the model can read every failure.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You'll extend the framework with a new tool and two new toolboxes.
The checks use a fake model. You've finished when you see 5 passed.

scenes.title: You opened the tool system.
points: A function already holds its schema
Toolbox sends failures back as text

captions.text: Each tool is now written once, and it can't disagree with itself.
Next, you'll turn run_agent into a real runtime.
